title: KOS Terminology Glossary
description: Terminological resource containing terms with definitions for concepts related to Knowledge Organization System Resources
scopeNote: The KOS Terminology Glossary is a terminological resource containing terms with definitions for concepts related to Knowledge Organization System Resources. The terms are not specific to any particular KOS Type.
historyNote: The glossary was created by Ben Norton with many terms and definitions adopted from a variety of sources

terms.label: Authority File
terms.definition: A controlled vocabulary or official list that establishes, for consistency, the authoritative forms of headings, and the preferred terms or proper names to be used, when creating a catalogue or when indexing and searching a set of entities within a defined domain.

terms.label: Authority List
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary for use in naming particular entities consistently

terms.label: Categorization Scheme
terms.definition: Information content entity that characterizes some aggregate of entities as partitioned into distinct subgroups, thereby demarcating them as categories.

terms.label: Category
terms.definition: A grouping of terms that are semantically or statistically associated, but which do not constitute a strict hierarchy based on genus/species, parent/child, or part/whole relationships.

terms.label: Classification Scheme
terms.definition: A method of organization according to a set of pre-established principles, usually characterized by a notation system and a hierarchical structure of relationships among the entities.

terms.label: Classification Scheme Item
terms.definition: A component of content in a Classification Scheme. This may be a node in a taxonomy or ontology or a term in a thesaurus, etc.

terms.label: Classification System
terms.definition: Terminological resource which has characteristics of mutual exclusiveness and exhaustiveness to aggregate data to a pre-prescribed level of specialization for a specific purpose
terms.scopeNote: It usually includes hierarchical relations as well as definitions and rules for use but might not, as in the example simple classification of gender: Male, Female.

terms.label: Codelist
terms.definition: A type of controlled vocabulary that is comprised of a finite list of standard terms and meanings that represent the allowable values for a data item

terms.label: Controlled Vocabulary
terms.definition: A collection of selected words and phrases related to a particular domain of knowledge used to permit consistency of metadata annotation and improved retrieval following a search, in which homonyms, synonyms and similar ambiguities of meaning present in natural language are disambiguated.

terms.label: Data Dictionary
terms.definition: Centralized repository of information about data such as meaning, relationships to other data, origin, usage and format

terms.label: Data Element Concept
terms.definition: A concept that can be represented in the form of a data element, described independently of any particular representation

terms.label: Data Interchange Standard
terms.definition: A standard which defines a set of data according to a set of data structuring rules so that the set of data can be interchanged between one computer system and another

terms.label: Data Standard
terms.definition: A statement that defines conventions, guidelines, characteristics or methods for consistent data handling to facilitate exchange or processing of the data.
terms.scopeNote: The defining criteria for a data standard are reviewed by and agreed upon by the user community or a governing body before they are released and adopted for use.

terms.label: Dataset
terms.definition: A collection of related facts, often expressed in numerical form and encoded in a defined structure.

terms.label: Datatype
terms.definition: Set of distinct values, characterized by properties of those values, and by operations on those values

terms.label: Defined Term Set
terms.definition: A set of defined terms, for example a set of categories or a classification scheme, a glossary, dictionary or enumeration.

terms.label: Deliverable
terms.definition: A document containing a project report, intended to be delivered to a customer or funding agency describing the results achieved within a specific project.

terms.label: Described Value Domain
terms.definition: Value domain that is specified by a description or specification, such as a rule, a procedure or a range (i.e. interval)

terms.label: Discipline Dictionary
terms.definition: A discipline dictionary is a collection of subject disciplines.

terms.label: Enumerated Value Domain
terms.definition: Value domain that is specified by a list of all its permissible values

terms.label: Glossary
terms.definition: An alphabetical list of technical terms in some specialized field of knowledge; usually published as an appendix to a text on that field.

terms.label: Glossary Item
terms.definition: A Glossary Item records a business term that is commonly used within the metadata registry.

terms.label: Hierarchical Relationship
terms.definition: A relationship between or among terms in a controlled vocabulary that depicts broader (generic) to narrower (specific) or whole-part relationships; begins with the words broader term (BT), or narrower term (NT).

terms.label: Knowledge Organization System
terms.definition: All types of schemes for organizing information and promoting knowledge management. Knowledge organization systems include classification schemes that organize materials at a general level (such as books on a shelf), subject headings that provide more detailed access, and authority files that control variant versions of key information (such as geographic names and personal names). They also include less-traditional schemes, such as semantic artifacts, semantic networks and ontologies.

terms.label: List
terms.definition: A limited set of terms arranged as a simple alphabetical list or in some other logically evident way; containing no relationships of any kind

terms.label: Metadata
terms.definition: A separate work that provides information describing one or more characteristics of a resource or entity.

terms.label: Metadata Standard
terms.definition: A set of formally agreed guidelines defining the structure, content, and semantics necessary to make data understandable, discoverable, and interoperable

terms.label: Minimum Information Standard
terms.definition: A metadata standard specifying items to be included when creating metadata describing a dataset of a particular type, or when creating a structured summary of the main findings of an article or report in a particular domain of interest, thereby ensuring adequate descriptive information is recorded for subsequent resource discovery and/or interpretation of the information described.

terms.label: Narrower Term
terms.definition: A term that is subordinate to another term or to multiple terms in a hierarchy. In thesauri, the relationship indicator for this type of term is NT.

terms.label: Ontology
terms.definition: A formal model that allows knowledge to be represented for a specific domain. An ontology describes the types of things that exist (classes), the relationships between them (properties) and the logical ways those classes and properties can be used together (axioms).

terms.label: Permissible Value
terms.definition: Designation of a value meaning

terms.label: Pick List
terms.definition: A graphical user interface device that allows the user to select from a pre-set list of terms. Typically the list of terms is shown when the user clicks on a down arrow next to the entry box for the term.

terms.label: Standard
terms.definition: A specification giving a precise statement of a process or a service requirement, often sanctioned by a nation or industry. A document describing a standard.

terms.label: Taxonomy
terms.definition: A classification arranged in a hierarchical structure of classes and subclasses, showing parent-child isA relationships, or broader_than - narrower_than relationships.

terms.label: Terminological Dictionary
terms.definition: Terminology resource that is designed to be used as a reference work

terms.label: Thesaurus
terms.definition: Controlled and structured vocabulary in which concepts are represented by terms, organized so that relationships between concepts are made explicit, and preferred terms are accompanied by lead-in entries for synonyms or quasi-synonyms

terms.label: Tree Structure
terms.definition: A controlled vocabulary display format in which the complete hierarchy of terms is shown. Each term is assigned a tree number or line number which leads from the alphabetical display to the hierarchical one. The hierarchical display is also known as systematic display.

terms.label: Type Vocabulary
terms.definition: An atomized set of terms that characterize the nature of a resource

terms.label: Uncontrolled Vocabulary
terms.definition: A non-defined collection of words and phrases relating to a particular domain of knowledge, usually added freely by a community, in which homonyms, synonyms and similar ambiguities of meaning present in natural language are not formally disambiguated.

terms.label: Value Domain
terms.definition: A resource type used to denote a collection of permissible values associated with a conceptual domain or term in a controlled vocabulary.
terms.scopeNote: Synonyms include codelist, value list, pick list, enumerated domain, and enumerated value set. Also defined in ISO/IEC 11179-3 as a class each instance of which models a value domain — a set of permissible values — providing representation without implication as to the associated Data Element Concept.

terms.label: Vocabulary
terms.definition: Terminological dictionary which contains designations and definitions for one or more specific subject fields.
terms.scopeNote: Also defined as: a set of words constituting a language or used to describe a particular domain of knowledge (FaBiO); a collection of terms for a particular purpose (W3C LD Glossary).

terms.label: Vocabulary Mapping
terms.definition: A mapping of correspondences between two vocabularies. For controlled vocabularies, such mappings may be expressed using SKOS (http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/).

sources.title: Bibliographic Ontology (BIBO)
sources.description: BIBO is an ontology for the bibliographic description of documents, books, and articles used to represent citations and bibliographic references on the Semantic Web.

sources.title: COAR Resource Types Vocabulary
sources.description: The Confederation of Open Access Repositories (COAR) Controlled Vocabularies are used to describe the type and access rights of open access resources.

sources.title: FRBR-aligned Bibliographic Ontology (FaBiO)
sources.description: FaBiO is an ontology for recording and publishing on the Semantic Web descriptions of entities that are published or potentially publishable, and that contain or are referred to by bibliographic references.

sources.title: The Interconnected Data Dictionary Ontology (IDDO)
sources.description: The IDDO maps the data model of ISO 23386 for the describing, creating, and maintenance of properties in interconnected data dictionaries.

Ontology for Modeling and Representation of Social Entities
sources.description: The OMRSE is an OBO Foundry ontology that represents the various entities that arise from human social interactions, such as social acts, social roles, social groups, and organizations.

sources.title: Schema.org
sources.description: Schema.org is a collaborative community activity with a mission to create, maintain, and promote schemas for structured data on the Internet.

sources.title: This Document
sources.description: Term defined in-house by the editorial group; no external source.

sources.title: VIVO Ontology for Researcher Discovery
sources.description: The VIVO ontology represents researchers in the context of their experience, outputs, interests, accomplishments, and associated institutions.

sources.title: Vocabulary of a Friend (VOAF)
sources.description: VOAF is a vocabulary specification providing elements allowing the description of vocabularies used in the Linked Data Cloud. It provides properties expressing the different ways vocabularies can rely on, extend, specify, annotate or otherwise link to each other.
